en.deck: Toronto has lost seven straight, scoring 1.6 goals a game over its last five, and just became the first Leafs team to go through a six-game homestand without a point. en.title: Hughes and Kaprizov carry matching 12-game point streaks into Calgary
en.deck: Minnesota is 16-3-4, has won four straight and has a point in 12 straight games, and Quinn Hughes and Kirill Kaprizov have scored in all 12. Calgary won the first meeting 2-1 and beat San Jose on Tuesday. Both sides make the Wild clear favourites, but the market more so than the model.
news: Hughes has 19 points during his streak, a career best and a franchise record. He has 7 goals and 25 assists in 23 games.
Filip Gustavsson has been medically cleared and will play one AHL game before rejoining the Wild on this trip. Jesper Wallstedt is the likely starter.
Brock Faber and Jonathan Marchessault are back in the lineup.
Calgary is without Jonathan Huberdeau (hip), and Kevin Bahl is out for the season.
records: Wallstedt is 15-2-3 with a 1.99 goals-against average and a .924 save percentage.
Minnesota has scored six or more in two straight games and is 10-3-2 on the road.
Joel Eriksson Ek passed Ryan Suter for seventh in Wild history in points (371).
The last 10 meetings averaged only 5.3 goals.

en.title: Colorado plays without MacKinnon and Makar on the second night of a back-to-back
en.deck: Colorado lost 4-1 in Utah on Wednesday and plays again a day later, still without Nathan MacKinnon (out about a month) and Cale Makar (about two weeks). Anaheim has the league's best power play and has scored 4.2 goals a game over its last five. The model makes Colorado a bigger favourite than the market does.
news: MacKinnon and Makar were both hurt on Nov. 12 in Ottawa. Colorado claimed defenceman Mike Reilly off waivers from Carolina.
Mackenzie Blackwood started in Utah, so Scott Wedgewood (1-3-2) may get the net. Wedgewood is six wins from 100.
Josh Manson and Zachary L'Heureux are also out for Colorado.
Ducks: Leo Carlsson leads the team with 27 points and Cutter Gauthier has 18 goals. Ryan Poehling and A.J. Greer are on injured reserve.
records: Anaheim's power play converts 36%, the best in the NHL.
Ducks games have gone over 5.5 goals 86% of the time this season.
Lukas Dostal has an .858 save percentage, among the lowest of the regular starters.
Parker Kelly is two points from 100 in his career, and Nicolas Roy two from 200.

en.title: The Canucks bring their first winning streak of the season to Seattle
en.deck: Vancouver is last in the Pacific at 5-17-1 but has won two straight on the road, its first winning streak this season. Seattle has lost three straight, including two lopsided losses to Carolina in Finland. The Kraken are 7-0-2 in their last nine games against Vancouver, and both model and market favour them.
news: Leevi Merilainen should start for Vancouver after Nikita Tolopilo was sent to Abbotsford. Merilainen made 34 saves in the 6-3 win in Vegas.
Philipp Grubauer is Seattle's projected starter. Joey Daccord was pulled after allowing four goals on 14 shots in the 5-1 loss in Finland.
Marco Rossi centres Vancouver's fourth line, and Jake DeBrusk took a maintenance day on Wednesday.
It is Manny Malhotra's first season as Vancouver's coach; Lane Lambert coaches Seattle.

en.title: Stars and Golden Knights meet again two nights after an overtime thriller
en.deck: Dallas won 4-3 in overtime in Las Vegas on Tuesday: Mikko Rantanen tied it with five seconds left and Miro Heiskanen won it in his return from injury. The Stars have won three straight, while Vegas has lost three in a row (0-1-2) under first-year coach Ryan Craig. Model and market both lean slightly to Vegas.

Jamie Benn reached 1,000 career points on Nov. 15.
Dallas is without Lian Bichsel and Tyler Myers.
Craig took over from John Tortorella in June, after Vegas lost in the Stanley Cup Final. Neither starting goalie is confirmed.
records: Jake Oettinger (11-4-1, 2.22) leads the NHL with four shutouts.
